💰 Big Tech Now Owes $2 Trillion To The A.I. Boom; Number Officially Leaves The Chart

WALL STREET — filed in a currency we can no longer read

MARKETS — Big tech companies are now sitting on a combined $2 trillion in spending commitments for the AI boom — a figure so large economists have stopped using dollars and started describing it in terms of "several moons."

"It's a very confident number," one analyst said, gazing at a spreadsheet that had quietly caught fire. Executives insist the investment will pay off, right after this next datacenter, and the one after that, and possibly one small dedicated sun.

🌍 Google Pulls A.I. Earth Tool After It Adds Places That Don't Exist; Cartographers Weep

MOUNTAIN VIEW — reported from a lake that wasn't there yesterday

OOPS — Google rolled back an AI-powered Earth feature after it began generating images of things that were not, technically, real — inventing lakes, relocating mountains, and confidently placing a dense forest where there is, in fact, a Denny's.

"It was being creative," an engineer offered weakly, as users discovered their landlocked hometown now has a coastline. Geographers noted this is the first mapping tool that requires both a fact-checker and a therapist.

🦘 Australia Makes Big Tech Pay For News; Tech Reveals It Never Read The News Anyway

CANBERRA — filed with all the appropriate paperwork

REGULATION — Australia expanded its demand that big tech companies pay publishers for news stories — a rule the platforms are grappling with by insisting they were mostly showing headlines to people who were never going to click them.

"We deeply value journalism," a spokesperson said, having never once opened an article past the first sentence. Negotiations are ongoing, tense, and being live-blogged by three outlets that will also need to be paid.

SOMEWHERE WEARABLE — reported at arm's length

GADGETS — A new smart ring, the Index 01, features a button you press to talk to its AI assistant whenever there's something you want to remember — finally outsourcing human memory to jewelry, exactly the way nature intended.

SILICON VALLEY — reported through a slightly ajar door

SECURITY — Reports of cybersecurity stumbles at leading AI labs are raising fresh concerns, proving that the companies building superintelligent machines are, reassuringly, just as capable as the rest of us at leaving a digital door unlatched.

"We take security extremely seriously," the labs said in unison, from behind a password that was, briefly, 'password.' Experts note there is something deeply humbling about a system that can pass the bar exam and still gets phished on a quiet Tuesday.
